# awscc_ses_email_identity_certificate (Resource)

Associates an AWS Certificate Manager certificate with a sender under an SES email identity, so that SES signs the sender's mail with S/MIME. Removing this resource removes only the association. The ACM certificate itself stays intact. SES stores the sender lower-cased, and this provider matches senders case-insensitively and preserves the casing from the template.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `certificate_arn` (String) The ARN of the AWS Certificate Manager certificate to associate with the sender.
- `email_identity` (String) The email identity that owns the sender the certificate is associated with.
- `from_address` (String) The sender the certificate signs for. For an email address identity this is the identity itself.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_ses_email_identity_certificate.example
  identity = {
    email_identity = "email_identity"
    from_address   = "from_address"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `email_identity` (String) The email identity that owns the sender the certificate is associated with
- `from_address` (String) The sender the certificate signs for

#### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AWS Account where this resource is managed
- `region` (String) Region where this resource is managed

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_ses_email_identity_certificate.example
  id = "email_identity|from_address"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import awscc_ses_email_identity_certificate.example "email_identity|from_address"
```
